name: codex-project-memory-edit-v1
recipe: conda prefix from the 39 sha256-pinned conda-forge packages of the paper environment; cargo-home either from the pinned archive of the paper environment (if AGENTSWE_ENV_ARCHIVE_DIR holds it) or by `cargo fetch --locked` of a0's codex-rs/Cargo.lock (identical in zh-asrun and en-upstream a0, retried and resumable) plus the rusty_v8 v150.4.0 release asset (sha256 5869fdb7...)
parity_with_paper: rebuilt on 123 (10-03): conda prefix 91,458 files identical, 345 differ only by the install prefix (183 text, 162 binary), one .pyc and two empty cargo bookkeeping files differ; cargo-home crate cache 1,155/1,155 .crate files and the 6 git dependency checkouts byte-identical; rusty_v8: the paper held a locally recompressed .gz of the same library (decompressed sha256 453df876... identical; compressed bytes differ)
used_as: the evaluator's offline Rust toolchain: harbor/build_preflight.py builds the unchanged a0 and every Candidate with <env>/bin/cargo inside bubblewrap (--unshare-all, compiler read-only), CARGO_HOME=<env>/cargo-home copied per build, OPENSSL_DIR=<env>
not_reproduced: paper-environment directories the evaluator never reads: cargo/ (an earlier CARGO_HOME, 1.5 GB), npm-cache/, bootstrap-assets/
notes: Built on the host, not in a container: the trees reference @@AGENTSWE_ENVS@@/codex-project-memory-edit-v1 and run its cargo from host paths. a0 must be fetched first (setup does). The link step uses the host C compiler (cc), as in the paper. Fetching about 1,150 crates from crates.io can be slow from some networks; AGENTSWE_BUILD_PROXY is honoured.
